newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China foils hijack attempt in Guangzhou - reports.
newsitem.headline: China foils hijack attempt in Guangzhou - reports.

text.p: China foiled the attempted hijacking of a domestic airliner in the south of the country, and the aircraft and all of its passengers were safe, a pro-Beijing newspaper in Hong Kong reported on Tuesday.
The attempted hijacking occurred on Monday at Baiyun airport in Guangzhou, the capital of Guangdong province, the China-controlled Wen Wei Po said.

"Baiyun airport yesterday dealt with a case of hijacking," it said. "Preliminary information shows it was a passenger aircraft from another province's airline. The aircraft and the people are now all safe," it said.
The newspaper gave no further details.

But the independent Hong Kong daily Ming Pao said in a report from Guangzhou the hijacker had been subdued after a struggle while the plane was in flight and that it later landed safely at Baiyun aipport, where all passengers disembarked unhurt.
Ming Pao said the motives of the hijacking and the identity of the hijacker were not yet known. It gave no other details.
The newspaper said it was the first airplane hijacked in China in two years. Before that, Chinese airlines had suffered a spate of hijackings, mainly by people trying to flee to Taiwan.
